title: Loss of CHGA Protein as a Potential Biomarker for Colon Cancer Diagnosis: A Study on Biomarker Discovery by Machine Learning and Confirmation by Immunohistochemistry in Colorectal Cancer Tissue Microarrays
summary: Machine-learning screening of protein-interaction candidates selected CHGA as a colorectal-cancer biomarker; the study reports AUC 0.90 in microarray data, 0.995 in RNA-seq data and immunohistochemistry across 198 specimens. This supports a candidate biomarker association, not prospective screening benefit.
ai_technology: Machine learning screens protein-interaction candidates; CHGA is selected and evaluated in tissue arrays.
organization: Institute of Medical Sciences, School of Medicine, Örebro University, 702 81 Örebro, Sweden

evidence.tested: Results reports AUC 0.90 microarray, 0.995 RNA-seq and IHC across 198 specimens; follow-up is candidate biomarker evidence.
evidence.unknown: Evidence supports a candidate biomarker association; prospective screening and clinical outcomes were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning screens protein-interaction candidates; CHGA is selected and evaluated in tissue arrays.
